title: A New Race to the Moon

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店当DJ的黑胶唱片时代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的收藏品去工作，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Last week, when India landed a spacecraft on the moon, it revealed just how much the international space race has changed.
sentences.zh: 上周，当印度航天器在月球着陆时，它揭示了国际太空竞赛已经发生了多大的变化。

sentences.en: Today, I speak with my colleague Kenneth Chang about why a new set of players is dominating that race and what is motivating their groundbreaking missions to the moon.
sentences.zh: 今天，我将与我的同事肯尼斯·张探讨为什么一批新的参与者正在主导这场竞赛，以及是什么在激励他们进行这些开创性的登月任务。

sentences.en: It's Monday, August 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月28日，星期一。

sentences.en: Ken, I wonder if you can just describe the t-shirt you're wearing.
sentences.zh: 肯，我想请你描述一下你身上穿的这件T恤。

sentences.en: I just happened to be wearing my NASA t-shirt.
sentences.zh: 我正好穿了这件NASA的T恤。

sentences.en: It was from 2018 when it was the sixth anniversary of NASA.
sentences.zh: 这是2018年NASA成立60周年时出的。

sentences.en: You just happened to be wearing that?
sentences.zh: 你正好穿了这件？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I wasn't even looking.
sentences.zh: 我甚至都没特意找。

sentences.en: Is it possible your NASA t-shirt is in very frequent circulation on your body?
sentences.zh: 有没有可能你这件NASA T恤的出镜率太高了？

sentences.en: I probably should change more often, yes.
sentences.zh: 我确实应该换得勤一点，没错。

sentences.en: Ken, I want to start by asking you to describe this moment that unfolded out there in space last week.
sentences.zh: 肯，我想先请你描述一下上周在太空中发生的那个时刻。

sentences.en: India had this robotic space probe in orbit around the moon.
sentences.zh: 印度当时有一个机器人探测器正在绕月飞行。

sentences.en: And last week, it took the momentous last step in attempting to land it on the moon near the South Pole.
sentences.zh: 上周，它迈出了关键的最后一步，尝试在月球南极附近着陆。

sentences.en: After arriving in lunar orbit, it's sort of been slowly changing its orbit to get ready for this landing.
sentences.zh: 在进入月球轨道后，它一直在缓慢调整轨道，为这次着陆做准备。

sentences.en: And on what was Wednesday morning for me, it started firing its engines for the last time.
sentences.zh: 对我来说是周三早上的时候，它最后一次点燃了发动机。

sentences.en: At this point, it's slowing down and falling to the moon.
sentences.zh: 此时，它正在减速并向月球坠落。

sentences.en: And there's no turning back now.
sentences.zh: 现在已经没有回头路了。

sentences.en: It either has to land or crash.
sentences.zh: 它要么成功着陆，要么坠毁。

sentences.en: There's no other choice.
sentences.zh: 没有别的选择。

sentences.en: A very good evening to all of you.
sentences.zh: 大家晚上好。

sentences.en: We at ISRO welcome you to the live coverage of India's prestigious Chandrayaan 3 missions landing event on the lunar surface.
sentences.zh: 我们印度空间研究组织（ISRO）欢迎各位收看印度“月船3号”任务在月球表面着陆的现场直播。

sentences.en: So the Indian Space Agency is making this live stream broadcast of the landing.
sentences.zh: 所以印度航天局正在对这次着陆进行现场直播。

sentences.en: So we're seeing everyone in the control room.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了控制室里的每一个人。

sentences.en: The scientists here at ISTRAC are glued to their systems, analyzing all sorts of complex data.
sentences.zh: ISTRAC的科学家们正全神贯注地盯着系统，分析各种复杂的数据。

sentences.en: And like millions of people around the world, I was watching it on my computer.
sentences.zh: 和全世界数百万人一样，我当时也在电脑前看着。

sentences.en: And they're now seeing each step along the way.
sentences.zh: 他们现在正看着每一个步骤的进展。

sentences.en: Currently, only two engines are now being fired.
sentences.zh: 目前，只有两台发动机在工作。

sentences.en: The engines are firing.
sentences.zh: 发动机正在点火。

sentences.en: We are nearly at zero velocity.
sentences.zh: 我们几乎达到了零速度。

sentences.en: Its velocity, its descent rate.
sentences.zh: 它的速度，它的下降率。

sentences.en: We were hovering and now we are approaching the moon's surface.
sentences.zh: 我们刚才还在悬停，现在正在接近月球表面。

sentences.en: It continues to descend.
sentences.zh: 它继续下降。

sentences.en: We can see the Honorable Prime Minister, Srinarendra Modi Ji, who is here to encourage us.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到尊敬的总理纳伦德拉·莫迪先生，他来到这里为我们加油。

sentences.en: Prime Minister Modi of India pops up on the screen.
sentences.zh: 印度总理莫迪出现在屏幕上。

sentences.en: He's in South Africa for a meeting, but he wants to be there, at least virtually, during this historic event.
sentences.zh: 他当时正在南非参加会议，但他希望至少以虚拟方式参与这一历史性时刻。

sentences.en: And we are approaching the vertical descent phase 2, which will...
sentences.zh: 我们正在接近垂直下降的第二阶段，这将……

sentences.en: It slows down.
sentences.zh: 它减速了。

sentences.en: It stops for a moment at this height of 150 meters.
sentences.zh: 它在150米的高度停顿了一下。

sentences.en: Just for last minute checks.
sentences.zh: 只是为了做最后的检查。

sentences.en: And it descends the remaining 150 meters.
sentences.zh: 然后它下降了剩下的150米。

sentences.en: India is at the brink of creating history, as we all await with bated breath to witness the landing on Moon's South Polar region.
sentences.zh: 印度正处于创造历史的边缘，我们都屏息以待，见证着陆在月球南极地区。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: All of a sudden, there's cheering breaking out in mission control.
sentences.zh: 突然间，任务控制中心爆发出欢呼声。

sentences.en: Modi's waving his Indian flag.
sentences.zh: 莫迪挥舞着印度国旗。

sentences.en: Sir, we have achieved soft landing on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 先生，我们已经实现了在月球上的软着陆。

sentences.en: India is on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 印度登月了。

sentences.en: And it's one part pure exuberance and joy, and one part relief.
sentences.zh: 这既有纯粹的兴奋和喜悦，也有一份如释重负。

sentences.en: I request our Honorable Prime Minister to address us and bless us.
sentences.zh: 我请求我们尊敬的总理致辞并给予我们祝福。

sentences.en: Thank you, sir.
sentences.zh: 谢谢您，先生。

sentences.en: India's successful Moon mission is not just India's alarm.
sentences.zh: 印度成功的登月任务不仅仅是印度的骄傲。

sentences.en: India was the first country to successfully land near the South Pole of the Moon.
sentences.zh: 印度是第一个成功在月球南极附近着陆的国家。

sentences.en: This success belongs to all of humanity.
sentences.zh: 这一成功属于全人类。

sentences.en: Ken, this is clearly an accomplishment.
sentences.zh: 肯，这显然是一项成就。

sentences.en: But with all due respect to India, this was a robotic spacecraft landing on the Moon 50 years after the United States did something arguably much harder,
sentences.zh: 但恕我直言，这只是一个机器人航天器在着陆，而美国在50年前做了一件可以说难得多得多的事情，

sentences.en: which is put humans on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 那就是把人类送上月球。

sentences.en: So, why is India even undertaking this mission now?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么印度现在还要进行这项任务呢？

sentences.en: And why is it being treated as such a big moment?
sentences.zh: 为什么它被视为如此重要的时刻？

sentences.en: So, you're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: This doesn't compare to what NASA did during the space program when I was young.
sentences.zh: 这确实无法与我年轻时NASA太空计划所做的事情相比。

sentences.en: But it's a completely different space race.
sentences.zh: 但这完全是一场不同的太空竞赛。

sentences.en: Now, it's everyone, including India, wanting to go to the Moon.
sentences.zh: 现在，包括印度在内的每个人都想去月球。

sentences.en: And they're going to a completely different part of the Moon.
sentences.zh: 而且他们要去的是月球一个完全不同的地方。

sentences.en: It's near the South Pole.
sentences.zh: 就在南极附近。

sentences.en: And that offers a whole new range of opportunities and scientific mysteries that no one has tried to answer yet.
sentences.zh: 那提供了一系列全新的机遇和科学谜题，还没有人尝试去解答。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 解释一下。

sentences.en: Why is this such a different kind of competition to get to the Moon and a different set of opportunities?
sentences.zh: 为什么这是一种如此不同的登月竞争，又有着怎样不同的机遇？

sentences.en: So, NASA wrapped up its Apollo Moon landings in 1972.
sentences.zh: NASA在1972年结束了阿波罗登月计划。

sentences.en: And one of the amazing things they did was bring back rocks and dirt from the Moon.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的最了不起的事情之一就是带回了月球的岩石和土壤。

sentences.en: And that's been a treasure trove for scientists to understand the history of the solar system.
sentences.zh: 这对科学家了解太阳系的历史来说是一个宝库。

sentences.en: But after that, people sort of felt, you know, the Moon, we've been there, we've done that, we've brought back the rocks and dirt,
sentences.zh: 但那之后，人们觉得，你知道，月球我们已经去过了，做过了，带回了岩石和土壤，

sentences.en: we've basically learned everything that we need to know about the Moon.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上已经了解了关于月球我们需要知道的一切。

sentences.en: And so, NASA and planetary scientists want something new.
sentences.zh: 所以，NASA和行星科学家们想要新的东西。

sentences.en: So, they are looking toward Mars, to Venus.
sentences.zh: 于是他们看向火星、金星。

sentences.en: They sent the Voyager spacecraft that went past Jupiter and Saturn and produced all these amazing new images of these new planets.
sentences.zh: 他们发射了旅行者号探测器，飞过了木星和土星，并拍摄了这些新行星令人惊叹的新照片。

sentences.en: And for decades, people kind of just overlooked the Moon.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，人们基本上忽略了月球。

sentences.en: It was just something that you looked up at night and perhaps noticed some craters, but it had been forgotten scientifically.
sentences.zh: 它只是你晚上抬头看时会注意到的东西，或许能看到一些陨石坑，但在科学上它已经被遗忘了。

sentences.en: But this started to change in the mid-1990s.
sentences.zh: 但这种情况在90年代中期开始改变。

sentences.en: There were radar images taken by the Arecibo Radio Telescope in Puerto Rico.
sentences.zh: 波多黎各的阿雷西博射电望远镜拍摄了一些雷达图像。

sentences.en: They bounced radar signals off the Moon.
sentences.zh: 他们向月球发射了雷达信号。

sentences.en: And there were certain places, particularly in the polar regions, where the reflections seemed particularly bright, as if there was something shiny,
sentences.zh: 在某些地方，特别是在极地地区，反射看起来特别亮，好像有什么闪闪发光的东西，

sentences.en: almost like ice at the bottom of this crater.
sentences.zh: 就像陨石坑底部的冰一样。

sentences.en: But there was no way to tell from the radar why these parts were so shiny.
sentences.zh: 但从雷达上无法判断为什么这些地方如此明亮。

sentences.en: And this just continued as a mystery, until there was one scientist named Alan Binder.
sentences.zh: 这个谜团一直持续着，直到有一位名叫艾伦·宾德的科学家出现。

sentences.en: He had this proposal for sending a dirt-cheap spacecraft to the Moon.
sentences.zh: 他提出了一个发送廉价航天器去月球的计划。

sentences.en: It was an orbiter, it didn't land.
sentences.zh: 那是一个轨道飞行器，不会着陆。

sentences.en: And it was called Lunar Prospector.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“月球勘探者”。

sentences.en: And he had to fight the NASA leadership because, like everyone else, NASA was looking to do things farther out in the solar system.
sentences.zh: 他不得不与NASA领导层抗争，因为像其他人一样，NASA当时正寻求在太阳系更远的地方开展工作。

sentences.en: The Moon would still have been there, done that.
sentences.zh: 月球依然是那种“去过、做过”的地方。

sentences.en: But Alan Binder finally won funding to do Lunar Prospector.
sentences.zh: 但艾伦·宾德最终赢得了“月球勘探者”的资金支持。

sentences.en: It orbited the Moon.
sentences.zh: 它绕月飞行。

sentences.en: And it was able to measure hydrogen, large amounts of hydrogen in certain parts of the Moon.
sentences.zh: 它能够测量氢，在月球的某些部分发现了大量的氢。

sentences.en: And for the first time, the pieces fit together.
sentences.zh: 第一次，这些碎片拼凑在了一起。

sentences.en: These places corresponded to where the scientists had previously seen the shiny spots on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 这些地方与科学家之前在月球上看到的闪亮斑点相对应。

sentences.en: And why is that important?
sentences.zh: 那为什么这很重要？

sentences.en: Hydrogen, the most likely form that this could be in, was H2O.
sentences.zh: 氢，最可能存在的形式是H2O。

sentences.en: Water, which is two hydrogens and one oxygen.
sentences.zh: 水，也就是两个氢原子和一个氧原子。

sentences.en: And it's important as at the poles because it's colder at the North and South Pole.
sentences.zh: 这在极地很重要，因为北极和南极更冷。

sentences.en: And these spots look to be at the bottom of these deep craters.
sentences.zh: 这些斑点看起来位于深陨石坑的底部。

sentences.en: And the sun never shines at the bottom of these craters.
sentences.zh: 太阳永远照不到这些陨石坑的底部。

sentences.en: So, these are literally some of the coldest places in the solar system, a few degrees above absolute zero.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些实际上是太阳系中最冷的地方，仅比绝对零度高几度。

sentences.en: So, if ice ever formed in these craters, they would never have a chance to melt.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果这些陨石坑里曾经形成过冰，它们就永远没有机会融化。

sentences.en: And so, the ice at the bottom of these craters, you can almost think of it as the freezer compartment of the solar system,
sentences.zh: 所以，这些陨石坑底部的冰，你可以把它看作是太阳系的冷冻室，

sentences.en: where the layers of frost slowly layered on top of each other over four and a half billion years.
sentences.zh: 霜层在45亿年间缓慢地一层层堆积在上面。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, suddenly, all these pieces that you say that are fitting together, the shiny images, the cold temperatures, the hydrogen,
sentences.zh: 所以突然间，你所说的这些拼凑在一起的碎片——闪亮的图像、寒冷的温度、氢，

sentences.en: suggest that there might be water, ice water, on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 都表明月球上可能存在水，冰水。

sentences.en: And why would that be so important?
sentences.zh: 那为什么这如此重要？

sentences.en: Because now, this makes this place a much more appealing place to send astronauts.
sentences.zh: 因为现在，这使得月球成为一个更具吸引力的宇航员目的地。

sentences.en: One, there's new scientific mysteries to be discovered here.
sentences.zh: 第一，这里有新的科学谜题等待发现。

sentences.en: How did this ice get here?
sentences.zh: 这些冰是怎么来的？

sentences.en: What form is it in?
sentences.zh: 它以什么形式存在？

sentences.en: And two, water is a crucial resource for astronauts.
sentences.zh: 第二，水是宇航员的关键资源。

sentences.en: And water is really heavy, so you don't want to be sending all of it from Earth all the time.
sentences.zh: 水非常重，所以你不想一直从地球运送所有的水。

sentences.en: So, if it's there at the Moon already, that makes setting up a lunar base that much easier.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果月球上已经有了水，那么建立月球基地就会容易得多。

sentences.en: And you can do other things with water.
sentences.zh: 而且你可以用水做其他事情。

sentences.en: You can split it apart into hydrogen and oxygen.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它分解成氢和氧。

sentences.en: With oxygen, that's air for people to breathe.
sentences.zh: 有了氧气，人们就可以呼吸。

sentences.en: And the hydrogen, you can use it as fuel for rockets or for fuel cells to power a lunar base.
sentences.zh: 而氢气，你可以用它作为火箭燃料，或者作为燃料电池为月球基地供电。

sentences.en: So, suddenly, in this discovery that there might be water on the Moon, you're saying scientists, researchers are seeing the possibility of maybe living on the Moon
sentences.zh: 所以突然间，在这个可能存在月球水的发现中，你是说科学家和研究人员看到了在月球上生活的可能性，

sentences.en: or having much longer stays on the Moon because water would power all the things that would be there, the machines, the humans, etc.
sentences.zh: 或者在月球上停留更长时间，因为水可以为那里的所有设施供能，包括机器、人类等等。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If there's water in the polar regions of the Moon, it becomes much easier to set up a lunar base there.
sentences.zh: 如果月球极地有水，在那里建立月球基地就容易多了。

sentences.en: You can think of scientists setting up a cabin in the woods, almoSt.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象科学家们在森林里搭了个小木屋，差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: It probably wouldn't be continually occupied, but astronauts would come there periodically.
sentences.zh: 它可能不会一直有人居住，但宇航员会定期去那里。

sentences.en: They could have the air and the water from the resources on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 他们可以利用月球上的资源获取空气和水。

sentences.en: And they spend a couple of weeks digging up rocks, doing some other studies, and then going back home.
sentences.zh: 他们花几周时间挖掘岩石，进行其他研究，然后回家。

sentences.en: It not only makes it easier, but there's also new things that you can try to do on the Moon that you couldn't do otherwise.
sentences.zh: 这不仅让事情变得更容易，而且你还可以尝试在月球上做以前做不到的事情。

sentences.en: And then there were two missions in 2008 and 2009 that confirmed that there was indeed water ice and not just hydrogen on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 后来在2008年和2009年的两次任务证实，月球上确实存在冰水，而不仅仅是氢。

sentences.en: So I think I now understand what's going on here.
sentences.zh: 我想我现在明白是怎么回事了。

sentences.en: This discovery of water opens up a whole new world of possibilities on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 水的发现为月球开启了一个充满可能性的全新世界。

sentences.en: Possibility of a colony, fuel for space exploration, water for the astronauts doing that, exploring to drink and live on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 建立殖民地的可能性、太空探索的燃料、宇航员饮用和生活的用水。

sentences.en: And this is what sparks this new race to the Moon you described at the beginning of our conversation.
sentences.zh: 这就是引发我们在对话开始时提到的这场新登月竞赛的原因。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's now definitely water ice on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 月球上现在绝对有冰水。

sentences.en: And this creates new interest to go back to the Moon.
sentences.zh: 这引发了重返月球的新兴趣。

sentences.en: But this time, the cast of characters is different.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，参与的角色不同了。

sentences.en: It's not just the United States and NASA anymore.
sentences.zh: 不再仅仅是美国和NASA了。

sentences.en: Everyone wants to go to the Moon.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想去月球。

sentences.en: And a new space race to the Moon also has implications for the geopolitics back on Earth.
sentences.zh: 而一场新的登月竞赛也对地球上的地缘政治产生了影响。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: Sixty super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 六十款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们大概是联盟中每年表现最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175周年，致力于帮助您了解世界，充实度过每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在就访问 nytimes.com/subscribe 订阅，享受特别优惠。

sentences.en: So, Ken, tell us more about this new race to the Moon and about the countries that are involved in it and dominating it.
sentences.zh: 那么，肯，请给我们详细讲讲这场新的登月竞赛，以及参与其中并占据主导地位的国家。

sentences.en: Well, NASA is still a big player in this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，NASA在这方面仍然是一个重要角色。

sentences.en: The interests in the South Pole and the water led President George W.
sentences.zh: 对南极和水的兴趣促使乔治·W·布什总统启动了一项登月计划。

sentences.en: Bush to start a Moon program.
sentences.zh: 布什总统启动了一项登月计划。

sentences.en: But the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但美国一直有些摇摆不定。

sentences.en: has sort of been waffling.
sentences.zh: 但美国一直有些摇摆不定。

sentences.en: President Obama canceled that Moon program.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马总统取消了那个登月计划。

sentences.en: And then President Trump started a new one called Artemis.
sentences.zh: 后来特朗普总统启动了一个名为“阿尔忒弥斯”的新计划。

sentences.en: And President Biden has continued that.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统延续了这一计划。

sentences.en: But all that waffling means NASA hasn't gotten back to the Moon yet.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些摇摆意味着NASA至今还没能重返月球。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Russia's space program has largely faded away.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，俄罗斯的太空计划已基本销声匿迹。

sentences.en: And this has opened the door to new players in this new Moon race.
sentences.zh: 这为这场新登月竞赛中的新参与者打开了大门。

sentences.en: That includes private companies and countries that in the past you wouldn't have thought of as powers in space.
sentences.zh: 这包括私营公司和那些过去你不会认为在太空领域有实力的国家。

sentences.en: Well, tell me about those new powers.
sentences.zh: 那么，跟我说说那些新势力吧。

sentences.en: First and foremost, there's China.
sentences.zh: 首先也是最重要的，是中国。

sentences.en: While China launched its first lunar rover this morning, the unmanned spacecraft is on its way to the Moon.
sentences.zh: 中国今天早上发射了首个月球探测器，无人航天器正在前往月球的途中。

sentences.en: So China has had this very steady program of exploration of the Moon.
sentences.zh: 所以中国一直有着非常稳健的月球探测计划。

sentences.en: China became the first country to land a space probe on the Moon in 37 years.
sentences.zh: 中国成为37年来第一个将太空探测器降落在月球上的国家。

sentences.en: And everyone wants to get to the South Pole with the water.
sentences.zh: 每个人都想去有水的南极。

sentences.en: But first, everyone has to prove you can land on the Moon at all.
sentences.zh: 但首先，每个人都必须证明自己确实能降落在月球上。

sentences.en: China's lunar rover has successfully landed on the far side of the Moon.
sentences.zh: 中国的月球探测器已成功在月球背面着陆。

sentences.en: And China has managed to do this three times in a row.
sentences.zh: 而且中国已经连续三次成功做到了这一点。

sentences.en: China has landed a robot spacecraft on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 中国已经将机器人航天器降落在月球上。

sentences.en: Now, it's the third time China's landed a probe on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 现在，这是中国第三次将探测器降落在月球上。

sentences.en: And it's now going to spend several days trying to scoop up around two kilograms of samples before heading back.
sentences.zh: 它现在将花费几天时间尝试采集约两公斤的样本，然后返回。

sentences.en: And they're the only ones with a perfect record.
sentences.zh: 而且他们是唯一保持着完美记录的国家。

sentences.en: They haven't landed at the South Pole yet, but that's in their future plans.
sentences.zh: 他们还没有在南极着陆，但这在他们未来的计划中。

sentences.en: I'm curious what makes the Chinese so successful at this.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇是什么让中国在这方面如此成功。

sentences.en: It's one of the advantages of not being a democracy.
sentences.zh: 这是非民主体制的优势之一。

sentences.en: They don't change the destination or the budget because there's been an election.
sentences.zh: 他们不会因为选举而改变目标或预算。

sentences.en: So China sets out this five-year space program, and they fund it steadily.
sentences.zh: 所以中国制定了五年太空计划，并稳步提供资金。

sentences.en: So they've done what they planned, and they've done it roughly when they said they're going to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们完成了计划，而且大致是在他们承诺的时间内完成的。

sentences.en: But as you said, they didn't make it to the South Pole where the water is.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，他们还没能到达有水的南极。

sentences.en: What about the other players now in this race?
sentences.zh: 现在这场竞赛中的其他参与者呢？

sentences.en: So there was an Israeli non-profit that tried to launch to the Moon in 2019.
sentences.zh: 曾有一个以色列非营利组织在2019年尝试发射登月。

sentences.en: We seem to have a problem with our main engine.
sentences.zh: 我们的主引擎似乎出了问题。

sentences.en: They unfortunately crashed.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，他们坠毁了。

sentences.en: Earlier this year, there was a Japanese company called iSpace that attempted to land on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，一家名为iSpace的日本公司尝试在月球着陆。

sentences.en: Now we lost the communication.
sentences.zh: 现在我们失去了通讯。

sentences.en: We have to assume that we could not complete the landing on the lunar surface.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不假设我们没能完成月球表面的着陆。

sentences.en: They crashed.
sentences.zh: 他们坠毁了。

sentences.en: Hmm, Russia.
sentences.zh: 嗯，俄罗斯。

sentences.en: They were trying to revive their space program with their first lunar mission since 1976.
sentences.zh: 他们试图通过自1976年以来的首次月球任务来重振他们的太空计划。

sentences.en: Now Russia's first lunar mission in nearly 50 years has ended in failure after its spacecraft crashed into the Moon.
sentences.zh: 现在，俄罗斯近50年来的首次月球任务以失败告终，其航天器撞向了月球。

sentences.en: They crashed.
sentences.zh: 他们坠毁了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And then there's India.
sentences.zh: 接下来是印度。

sentences.en: We're just waiting for the updates from the mission control room.
sentences.zh: 我们正在等待任务控制中心的最新消息。

sentences.en: They tried first in 2019.
sentences.zh: 他们曾在2019年尝试过。

sentences.en: India's attempt to make one giant leap ended at the final step of its unmanned mission to the Moon.
sentences.zh: 印度试图迈出一大步的尝试，在其无人登月任务的最后一步戛然而止。

sentences.en: They crashed.
sentences.zh: 他们坠毁了。

sentences.en: And so this week was essentially a redo of what they attempted to do in 2019.
sentences.zh: 所以本周基本上是他们2019年尝试的重演。

sentences.en: And this time, they were successful in landing near the South Pole.
sentences.zh: 而这一次，他们成功在南极附近着陆了。

sentences.en: Ken, why is it so hard for all these countries and companies to get to the South Pole of the Moon?
sentences.zh: 肯，为什么所有这些国家和公司要到达月球南极都这么难？

sentences.en: I mean, when I think back to the 50-year journey we've been on since NASA landed on the Moon, it would seem like it shouldn't be that hard to get to any part of the Moon.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，回想一下NASA登月以来的50年历程，似乎到达月球的任何部分都不应该那么难。

sentences.en: The magic word that people use these days is sustainable.
sentences.zh: 人们现在用的神奇词汇是“可持续”。

sentences.en: So everyone wants to get to the Moon, but they want to do it on a budget.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都想去月球，但他们想在预算范围内完成。

sentences.en: And that's been sort of a tricky balance.
sentences.zh: 这一直是一种微妙的平衡。

sentences.en: So in the 60s, NASA spent billions of dollars for the Moon landings.
sentences.zh: 在60年代，NASA为登月花费了数十亿美元。

sentences.en: And if you spent that much money again, you would have a very, very good chance of succeeding on landing on the Moon.
sentences.zh: 如果你再次投入那么多钱，你将有非常、非常大的机会成功登月。

sentences.en: But all these new companies and these emerging space nations, they're trying to do it on a much cheaper price tag.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些新公司和新兴航天国家，他们试图以更低的价格完成任务。

sentences.en: And that's sort of been a compromise of how much technology you use, how much testing you have.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上是对技术使用量和测试量的妥协。

sentences.en: And they haven't been able to get that right on the first try.
sentences.zh: 而且他们没能在第一次尝试时就做好。

sentences.en: Right, because it turns out it's pretty hard to land on the Moon on a shoestring, which is pretty intuitive.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为事实证明，在资金拮据的情况下登月是相当困难的，这很直观。

sentences.en: But it sounds like it's been a very painful lesson for all of these entities.
sentences.zh: 但听起来这对所有这些实体来说都是非常痛苦的教训。

sentences.en: Yes, it's also been painful watching them.
sentences.zh: 是的，看着他们失败也很痛苦。

sentences.en: So this clearly remains a very expensive and meaningful undertaking for anybody who wants to get to the Moon, especially a country that has lots of competing interests to balance.
sentences.zh: 所以对于任何想去月球的人来说，这显然仍然是一项非常昂贵且意义重大的事业，尤其是对于一个需要平衡许多相互竞争利益的国家而言。

sentences.en: And that makes me wonder what's really motivating all these companies, and especially these new entrants, China and India, to devote the resources required to do this.
sentences.zh: 这让我好奇，到底是什么在激励所有这些公司，尤其是中国和印度这些新进入者，投入所需的资源来做这件事。

sentences.en: And I understand that the promise of water on the Moon's surface is very tantalizing.
sentences.zh: 我理解月球表面存在水的承诺非常诱人。

sentences.en: And I get that getting there first and discovering the water and harnessing it would be a real coup.
sentences.zh: 我也明白，率先到达那里、发现水并加以利用将是一项真正的壮举。

sentences.en: But is something else driving all of this?
sentences.zh: 但还有其他因素在驱动这一切吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it's a huge moment of national pride when they succeed.
sentences.zh: 是的，当他们成功时，这是一种巨大的民族自豪感时刻。

sentences.en: And so for these countries, of course, they're not overtaking what NASA accomplished 50 years ago,
sentences.zh: 所以对于这些国家来说，当然，他们并不是要超越NASA50年前取得的成就，

sentences.en: but they're forging their own path that for them was not possible even 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 但他们正在开辟自己的道路，这在10年前对他们来说是不可能的。

sentences.en: So when India launched this latest mission to the Moon, the schoolchildren watched the launch in school because it was like a national holiday almoSt.
sentences.zh: 所以当印度发射这次最新的登月任务时，学生们在学校里观看了发射，因为这几乎就像国定假日一样。

sentences.en: And China similarly is using its space program to basically trump it that it's now one of the major powers.
sentences.zh: 同样，中国也在利用其太空计划来宣示它现在是主要大国之一。

sentences.en: It uses it to try to attract cooperation with countries in Africa.
sentences.zh: 它利用这一点来尝试吸引与非洲国家的合作。

sentences.en: It's saying, come fly with us.
sentences.zh: 它在说，来和我们一起飞吧。

sentences.en: We'll fly you to our space station.
sentences.zh: 我们会送你们去我们的空间站。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What you're saying is, it's not just a question of pride, which sounds important and it sounds quite lovely.
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，这不仅仅是一个自豪感的问题，虽然这听起来很重要，也相当美好。

sentences.en: This is about a country's ability to project its strength on the world stage and all the things that the projection of that strength might yield, which is immeasurable.
sentences.zh: 这是关于一个国家在世界舞台上投射其力量的能力，以及这种力量投射可能带来的所有不可估量的成果。

sentences.en: Indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: That's what the space race of the 60s was, and that's what the space race of the 2020s is going to be.
sentences.zh: 这就是60年代的太空竞赛，也是2020年代太空竞赛将要呈现的样子。

sentences.en: And Ken, maybe this is a silly question, but why the Moon?
sentences.zh: 肯，也许这是一个愚蠢的问题，但为什么是月球？

sentences.en: I mean, it is hugely expensive.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这极其昂贵。

sentences.en: The failure rate is very high.
sentences.zh: 失败率非常高。

sentences.en: There are so many ways for a country to establish its place on the global stage and its prowess relative to its rivals.
sentences.zh: 一个国家有太多方式来确立其在全球舞台上的地位及其相对于竞争对手的实力。

sentences.en: Ways that are cheaper and with a higher rate of success.
sentences.zh: 那些方式更便宜，成功率也更高。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But part of what attracts people to the Moon is that it isn't easy.
sentences.zh: 但吸引人们前往月球的部分原因在于它并不容易。

sentences.en: We choose to go to the Moon.
sentences.zh: 我们选择登月。

sentences.en: That goes back to the famous JFK speech.
sentences.zh: 这可以追溯到肯尼迪总统著名的演讲。

sentences.en: We choose to go to the Moon in this decade and do the other things.
sentences.zh: 我们选择在这个十年内登月并做其他事情。

sentences.en: Not because they are easy, but because they are hard.
sentences.zh: 不是因为它们简单，而是因为它们困难。

sentences.en: That we do these things because they are difficult.
sentences.zh: 我们做这些事是因为它们具有挑战性。

sentences.en: And the Moon has always been this object of imagination for people.
sentences.zh: 月球一直是人们想象的对象。

sentences.en: You see it every night.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都能看到它。

sentences.en: And it's something that's big enough that you feel like you can almost touch it, but it's so far away that actually getting there always seemed impossible.
sentences.zh: 它足够大，让你觉得几乎可以触碰到它，但它又如此遥远，以至于真正到达那里似乎总是不可能的。

sentences.en: And so being able to say you're there is almost like saying I can do the impossible.
sentences.zh: 所以能够说你到了那里，就像是在说我能完成不可能的事。

sentences.en: Well, Ken, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，肯，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Sunday, Russia officially confirmed the death of Yevgeny Purgosyan, the head of a Russian mercenary group who led a brief rebellion against the country's military.
sentences.zh: 周日，俄罗斯正式确认了叶夫根尼·普里戈任的死讯，他是俄罗斯雇佣兵集团的首领，曾领导了一场针对该国军方的短暂叛乱。

sentences.en: It was widely presumed that Purgosyan was killed in a plane crash last week.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍认为普里戈任上周在飞机失事中丧生。

sentences.en: But over the weekend, genetic testing gave Russian officials final verification.
sentences.zh: 但周末，基因检测给了俄罗斯官员最终的核实。

sentences.en: While the cause of the crash remains unknown,
sentences.zh: 虽然坠机原因尚不清楚，

sentences.en: Western officials suspect that it was likely the result of sabotage by the Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 西方官员怀疑这很可能是克里姆林宫蓄意破坏的结果。

sentences.en: And over the weekend, a white gunman carried out what police said was a racist shooting at a store in Jacksonville, Florida, killing three black people,
sentences.zh: 周末，一名白人枪手在佛罗里达州杰克逊维尔的一家商店实施了警方所说的种族主义枪击事件，造成三名黑人死亡，

sentences.en: including two customers and an employee.
sentences.zh: 其中包括两名顾客和一名员工。

sentences.en: Plainly put, this shooting was racially motivated and he hated black people.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，这次枪击事件是出于种族动机，他憎恨黑人。

sentences.en: The gunman, who described his racist motive in a set of manifestos, used an AR-15 style rifle, upon which he had drawn multiple swastikas.
sentences.zh: 这名枪手在一系列宣言中描述了他的种族主义动机，他使用了一把AR-15式步枪，上面画着多个纳粹万字旗。

sentences.en: And according to police, during the shooting, he ordered several white customers out of the store.
sentences.zh: 据警方称，在枪击过程中，他命令几名白人顾客离开商店。

sentences.en: This is a dark day in Jacksonville's history.
sentences.zh: 这是杰克逊维尔历史上黑暗的一天。

sentences.en: Any loss of life is tragic.
sentences.zh: 任何生命的丧失都是悲剧。

sentences.en: But the hate that motivated the shooter's killing spree adds an additional layer of heartbreak.
sentences.zh: 但驱使枪手进行杀戮狂潮的仇恨增添了额外的痛苦。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Claire Tennesketter,
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由克莱尔·坦内斯凯特制作，

sentences.en: Sydney Harper, Astha Chaturvedi, and Rob Zipko.
sentences.zh: 悉尼·哈珀、阿斯塔·查图尔维迪和罗布·齐普科参与制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Michael Benoit, with help from Patricia Willans.
sentences.zh: 由迈克尔·贝努瓦编辑，帕特里夏·威廉斯协助。

sentences.en: Contains original music by Marion Lozano, Dan Powell, and Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 包含玛丽恩·洛萨诺、丹·鲍威尔和克里斯·伍德的原创音乐。

sentences.en: And was also engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 并由克里斯·伍德进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landverk of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰德弗克创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Balbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种需要全黑环境才能睡觉的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会因为喝醉而昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？
